subject: Seaview Health POC — hosting options, success criteria & kickoff plan
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Seaview Health POC — hosting options, success criteria & kickoff plan

Samir / Jenna — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + a suggested path so we can get a trial running next week. Attaching a compact trial matrix (seaview_trial_matrix.xlsx) with options and owners.

Key success criteria (please confirm priority order):
- S1: Latency < 200ms token round-trip for typical 256-token prompts (infra SLA)
- S2: Endpoint accuracy / label F1 >= 0.92 on your seeded eval set
- S3: Data segregation: PHI must not leave your controlled network
- S4: Cost target: <$0.005 per generated token on steady-state

Hosting options (high-level):
1) Hosted (Redwood API) — fastest to stand up, we can load your prompts and run benchmarks same-day. Good for early functional validation, NOT recommended if PHI cannot leave your VPC.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved capacity in Redwood) — predictable performance, isolated tenant resources, accessible over the internet with IP allowlists. Fastest for iteration + observable metrics.
3) VPC/private trial (VPC peering or on-prem package) — full network control and PHI-safe; longer setup (1–3 weeks) due to network/security approvals.

Proposed evaluation plan / timeline (draft):
- 11/05 — align on success criteria (this email)
- 11/09 — confirm environment choice & kickoff date
- 11/12 — trial kickoff (initial data push + baseline runs)
- 11/16 — mid-point checkpoint (metrics + tuning)

If VPC will add 1–3 weeks, is there a way to run the functional pass in Hosted to parallelize work (de-id set) while IT works the VPC setup? Also looping procurement (procurement@seaviewhealth.com) for SOW cadence.

Samir — quick technical note on paths forward and what we can parallelize. Attached is a VPC network template (vpc_network_template.yaml) and a short digest of what the Dedicated Sandbox provides versus a full VPC trial.

Recommendation (practical):
- Run parallel: Hosted (with de-identified dataset) for functional validation + Dedicated Sandbox for performance/observability testing.
- Reserve VPC/prep only if you need PHI in the loop for right-of-production tests. VPC adds networking approvals and (usually) an infra ticket with security — Ben can own the checklist.

Tradeoffs:
- Hosted: fastest, but not PHI safe. Good to prove prompts and integrate quickly.
- Dedicated sandbox: fast (~48h provisioning), stable perf, cost predictable, limited network controls (IP allowlist).
- VPC: most secure, longer lead time (1–3 weeks), greater coordination with your IT.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachments: vpc_network_template.yaml

Appreciate the options — two requests from my side before we lock the path: 
1) Can you provide a short baseline performance run on Hosted with our de-id sample (latency numbers + token cost estimate)? We want concrete numbers to compare against Dedicated.
2) Our clinical team insists the primary success metric is model accuracy on the seeded eval set; latency is second. For the POC, please highlight how tuning steps map to improving F1 on our set.

Sample priority (our preference):
- Primary: S2 (F1 >= 0.92)
- Secondary: S1 (latency < 200ms)
